Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Let F be complete for a multiplicative absolute value and V a finite-dimensional normed F-vector space. For any basis $v_1,\ldots,v_n$, its coordinate sup norm $\|\sum a_iv_i\|_\infty=\max_i|a_i|$ is bounded above and below by positive multiples of the given norm. For $n=0$ both norms are zero. Work in exact real arithmetic. Let $n\ge1$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$, and let
$A=A^{\mathsf T}$ satisfy $x^{\mathsf T}Ax>0$ for every nonzero $x$.
Give $V$ the energy inner product $a(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ and norm
$\|x\|_A^2=a(x,x)$ of
[[def-energy-inner-product-and-norm-for-a-hermitian-positive-definite-matrix]].
An operator $S$ is $A$-self-adjoint when $a(Sx,y)=a(x,Sy)$ for all $x,y$;
it is positive when $a(Sx,x)>0$ for every nonzero $x$. An $A$-orthogonal
projection is an idempotent $A$-self-adjoint operator.
Let $\mathcal I$ be a finite ordered nonempty set and, for each
$i\in\mathcal I$, choose a full-column-rank prolongation
$R_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times n_i}$ with $1\le n_i\le n$, and put
$V_i=\operatorname{Ran}(R_i)$.
A one-level method has $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. A two-level method has
$\mathcal I=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$, where $R_0=P$ and $V_0$ is the designated
coarse space. Restriction of a global residual is $R_i^{\mathsf T}$ and
prolongation of a local coefficient vector is $R_i$. Define the local energy
matrix
$$A_i=R_i^{\mathsf T}AR_i.$$
When the coarse index $0$ is present, $A_0=P^{\mathsf T}AP$ is the Galerkin
coarse matrix of [[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]]. By
[[thm-galerkin-coarse-correction-is-energy-orthogonal-projector]], it is SPD
and the exact coarse solve is well-defined.

For each $i\in\mathcal I$, the exact local correction and additive
preconditioner are
$$ \Pi_i=R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}A, \qquad B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
When the spaces span $V$, the exact additive Schwarz preconditioned operator
is $BA=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\Pi_i$. For a fixed ordering of $\mathcal I$, a
multiplicative sweep applies its corrections in that order; if $0$ is present,
it is first. For an inexact additive method, replace each exact $A_i^{-1}$ by
the inverse of an SPD matrix $\widetilde A_i$ satisfying, for fixed
$0<\alpha\le\beta$,
$$ \alpha A_i\preceq \widetilde A_i\preceq\beta A_i, \qquad \widetilde B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_i\widetilde A_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
For symmetric matrices, $X\preceq Y$ means
$z^{\mathsf T}Xz\le z^{\mathsf T}Yz$ for every vector $z$. The order
inequalities define uniform local spectral equivalence in this pair. The
lemma [[lem-schwarz-local-matrices-are-well-defined]] proves the remaining
local inverse and well-definedness claims.

Let $A_h\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and let
$P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ have full column rank. Put
$A_H=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$. Then $A_H$ is symmetric positive definite, hence
invertible, and the map $C=I_n-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h$ of
[[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]] satisfies

$$C^2=C,\qquad CP=0,\qquad P^{\mathsf T}A_hC=0,\qquad C^{\mathsf T}A_h=A_hC.$$

Consequently $\operatorname{Ran}(C)=\operatorname{Ran}(P)^{\perp_{A_h}}$;
$C$ is the orthogonal projector onto that complement in the energy inner
product $\langle x,y\rangle_{A_h}:=x^{\mathsf T}A_hy$.

Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ be Hermitian positive definite, let $b\in\mathbb C^n$,
and let $\phi$ be the quadratic energy from
[[def-quadratic-energy-of-a-hermitian-positive-definite-linear-system]]. Then
the system $Ax=b$ has a unique solution $x_*$, and for every $x\in\mathbb C^n$
one has

$$\phi(x)-\phi(x_*)=\tfrac12\|x-x_*\|_A^2.$$

In particular, $x_*$ is the unique minimizer of $\phi$.

For matrices of the appropriate shapes and a scalar $\lambda$,

$$(A+B)^{\mathsf T}=A^{\mathsf T}+B^{\mathsf T},\qquad (\lambda A)^{\mathsf T}=\lambda A^{\mathsf T},\qquad (A^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}=A,$$

and

$$(AB)^{\mathsf T}=B^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}.$$

Thus transpose is linear and involutive and reverses products.

> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

For each coordinate pair, a coarse ordering hyperplane can meet the interior of a fine cube only when the two fine-cell indices agree; there it is the local equality hyperplane used by the fine Freudenthal triangulation. Thus the fine mesh refines the coarse mesh: every fine simplex lies in one coarse simplex; the coarse and fine cell sets need not satisfy literal set inclusion. The induced order triangulation on a coordinate face is the same from either incident cube, so the meshes match. The reference simplices come from finitely many coordinate permutations, so their shape-regularity constants are bounded by a number depending only on $d$. By [F3], the continuous P1 spaces are nested. Their boundary nodal values vanish; [F4] places both spaces in $H_0^1(\Omega)$.

Let $J_H$ be the face-average Scott–Zhang map of [F1], set $u_0=J_Hu_h$, and $w=u_h-u_0\in V_h$. Each coarse element patch $\omega_K$ meets only coarse cubes whose coordinate indices differ from that of $K$ by at most one. Thus at most $M_d=3^d d!$ coarse simplex patches contain a fixed point. Squaring and summing [F1] over the coarse mesh gives $\|w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_S H\|
abla u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}, \qquad \|
abla u_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C_S\|
abla u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ for a constant $C_S$ depending only on $d$ and shape regularity. The second inequality is the global stability part of [F1]. The stated Countable Choice assumption supplies the choice principle required by the Scott–Zhang and Sobolev-trace suppliers in [F1].

Work in exact real arithmetic. Let $n\ge1$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$, and let
$A=A^{\mathsf T}$ satisfy $x^{\mathsf T}Ax>0$ for every nonzero $x$.
Give $V$ the energy inner product $a(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ and norm
$\|x\|_A^2=a(x,x)$ of
[[def-energy-inner-product-and-norm-for-a-hermitian-positive-definite-matrix]].
An operator $S$ is $A$-self-adjoint when $a(Sx,y)=a(x,Sy)$ for all $x,y$;
it is positive when $a(Sx,x)>0$ for every nonzero $x$. An $A$-orthogonal
projection is an idempotent $A$-self-adjoint operator.
Let $\mathcal I$ be a finite ordered nonempty set and, for each
$i\in\mathcal I$, choose a full-column-rank prolongation
$R_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times n_i}$ with $1\le n_i\le n$, and put
$V_i=\operatorname{Ran}(R_i)$.
A one-level method has $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. A two-level method has
$\mathcal I=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$, where $R_0=P$ and $V_0$ is the designated
coarse space. Restriction of a global residual is $R_i^{\mathsf T}$ and
prolongation of a local coefficient vector is $R_i$. Define the local energy
matrix
$$A_i=R_i^{\mathsf T}AR_i.$$
When the coarse index $0$ is present, $A_0=P^{\mathsf T}AP$ is the Galerkin
coarse matrix of [[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]]. By
[[thm-galerkin-coarse-correction-is-energy-orthogonal-projector]], it is SPD
and the exact coarse solve is well-defined.

For each $i\in\mathcal I$, the exact local correction and additive
preconditioner are
$$ \Pi_i=R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}A, \qquad B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
When the spaces span $V$, the exact additive Schwarz preconditioned operator
is $BA=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\Pi_i$. For a fixed ordering of $\mathcal I$, a
multiplicative sweep applies its corrections in that order; if $0$ is present,
it is first. For an inexact additive method, replace each exact $A_i^{-1}$ by
the inverse of an SPD matrix $\widetilde A_i$ satisfying, for fixed
$0<\alpha\le\beta$,
$$ \alpha A_i\preceq \widetilde A_i\preceq\beta A_i, \qquad \widetilde B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_i\widetilde A_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
For symmetric matrices, $X\preceq Y$ means
$z^{\mathsf T}Xz\le z^{\mathsf T}Yz$ for every vector $z$. The order
inequalities define uniform local spectral equivalence in this pair. The
lemma [[lem-schwarz-local-matrices-are-well-defined]] proves the remaining
local inverse and well-definedness claims.

For the data of [[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]], every
$\Pi_i=R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}A$ is an $A$-orthogonal projection, meaning
an idempotent $A$-self-adjoint operator, with range $V_i$. Consequently, for every
$x\in V$,
$$ \|x\|_A^2=\|\Pi_i x\|_A^2+\|(I-\Pi_i)x\|_A^2, \qquad a(\Pi_i x,x)=\|\Pi_i x\|_A^2. $$

Use the data of [[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]] and
assume the local spaces span $V$. Suppose $0<C_0,C_1<\infty$ satisfy:

- for every $x\in V$, there are local vectors $z_i$ such that
  $x=\sum_iR_i z_i$ and $\sum_i z_i^{\mathsf T}A_i z_i\le C_0\|x\|_A^2$;
- for every tuple $(z_i)$,
  $\|\sum_iR_i z_i\|_A^2\le C_1\sum_i z_i^{\mathsf T}A_i z_i$.

For an $A$-self-adjoint positive operator $T$, define
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(T)=\inf_{x\ne0}\frac{a(Tx,x)}{a(x,x)},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(T)=\sup_{x\ne0}\frac{a(Tx,x)}{a(x,x)},\qquad \kappa_A(T)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}^A(T)}{\lambda_{\min}^A(T)}. $$
Then the exact additive Schwarz operator $T=BA$ is $A$-self-adjoint positive and
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(BA)\ge C_0^{-1},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(BA)\le C_1,\qquad \kappa_A(BA)\le C_0C_1. $$
If the inexact local matrices satisfy
$\alpha A_i\preceq\widetilde A_i\preceq\beta A_i$ for
$0<\alpha\le\beta$, then
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(\widetilde BA)\ge(\beta C_0)^{-1},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(\widetilde BA)\le C_1/\alpha,\qquad \kappa_A(\widetilde BA)\le(\beta/\alpha)C_0C_1. $$

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: For an arbitrary initial error $x$, set $e_{-1}=x$, $d_0=\Pi_0x$, and $e_0=x-d_0$. For $i=1,\ldots,m$, set $d_i=\Pi_i e_{i-1}$ and $e_i=e_{i-1}-d_i$. By [F2], each correction is orthogonal to its updated error, so telescoping gives $D:=\sum_{i=0}^m\|d_i\|_A^2 =\|x\|_A^2-\|e_m\|_A^2.$ Also $e_{i-1}=x-d_0-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}d_j$.

Fix a local index $i\ge1$ and set $b_i=\|\Pi_i x\|_A$, $c_i=\|d_i\|_A$, and $q_i=\|\Pi_i d_0\|_A$. Since $x=e_{i-1}+d_0+\sum_{j<i}d_j$ and $\Pi_i$ is an orthogonal projection, $a(\Pi_i x,e_{i-1})=a(\Pi_i x,\Pi_i e_{i-1})=a(\Pi_i x,d_i)$ and $a(\Pi_i x,d_0)=a(\Pi_i x,\Pi_i d_0)$. Thus $b_i^2=a(\Pi_i x,d_i)+a(\Pi_i x,\Pi_i d_0)+\sum_{j<i}a(\Pi_i x,d_j)$. The first term has absolute value at most $b_i c_i$ and the second at most $b_i q_i$ by [F4]; the remaining terms are at most $b_i\sum_{j<i}\epsilon_{ij}c_j$ by [A2]. If $b_i=0$ the resulting bound is immediate; otherwise divide by $b_i$ to obtain $b_i\le c_i+q_i+\sum_{j<i}\epsilon_{ij}c_j.$

Let $L$ be the strict lower-triangular part of $G$, and let $b,c,q\in\mathbb R^m$ have entries $b_i,c_i,q_i$. They are nonnegative and $0\le Lc\le Gc$ entrywise. Hence $\|Lc\|_2\le\|Gc\|_2\le\rho\|c\|_2$, and step 2.1 yields $\|b\|_2\le(1+\rho)\|c\|_2+\|q\|_2.$ Furthermore, by [F2], $\|q\|_2^2 =\sum_{i=1}^m a(\Pi_i d_0,d_0) =a\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\Pi_i d_0,d_0\right) \le a(Td_0,d_0) \le C_1\|d_0\|_A^2.$ The first inequality uses that $\Pi_0$ is positive semidefinite; the last is [F3].

By $(r+s)^2\le2r^2+2s^2$, steps 1.1 and 3.1 give $\sum_{i=0}^m\|\Pi_i x\|_A^2 =\|d_0\|_A^2+\|b\|_2^2 \le(1+2C_1)\|d_0\|_A^2 +2(1+\rho)^2\sum_{i=1}^m\|d_i\|_A^2 \le K D.$ The left side is $a(Tx,x)$, which [F3] bounds below by $C_0^{-1}\|x\|_A^2$. Thus $D\ge(C_0K)^{-1}\|x\|_A^2$. Since $D\le\|x\|_A^2$ by step 1.1, $C_0K\ge1$.

Step 1.1 now gives $\|E_{\mathrm{mult}}x\|_A^2 =\|e_m\|_A^2 =\|x\|_A^2-D \le\left(1-\frac1{C_0K}\right)\|x\|_A^2.$ Taking the supremum over nonzero $x$ proves the operator-norm bound; finiteness of $C_0,K$ makes the contraction factor strictly less than one.

At almost every point of $\Omega$, at most $N_0=7^d$ local subdomains are present by [F3] and the coordinate count in [[thm-two-level-p1-poisson-stable-decomposition]]. For any coarse component $v_0$ and local components $v_j$, at most $N_0+1$ gradients can be nonzero there. [F4] in the finite-dimensional Euclidean inner product gives the pointwise inequality $\left|
abla v_0+\sum_j
abla v_jight|^2 \le (1+N_0)\left( |
abla v_0|^2+\sum_j|
abla v_j|^2 ight)$. Integrating gives $\left\|
abla\left(v_0+\sum_jv_jight)ight\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2 \le (1+N_0)\left( \|
abla v_0\|_2^2+\sum_j\|
abla v_j\|_2^2 ight).$ Thus $C_1=1+N_0$ is a valid synthesis constant.

Set $\epsilon_{ij}=1$ when the interiors of $\Omega_i$ and $\Omega_j$ overlap in positive measure and $0$ otherwise, with $\epsilon_{ii}=1$. If the interiors are disjoint, local gradients have disjoint supports almost everywhere, so $a(v_i,v_j)=0$. If they overlap, [F4] gives $|a(v_i,v_j)|\le\|v_i\|_A\|v_j\|_A$. Thus this symmetric nonnegative matrix satisfies the pairwise overlap hypothesis. Since each padded cube has side at most $5a$, two cubes can intersect only when their coarse indices differ by at most five in each coordinate. Thus every row of the overlap matrix has at most $N_1=11^d$ nonzero entries. For any vector $x$, applying [F4] to the vectors $(\sqrt{\epsilon_{ij}})_j$ and $(\sqrt{\epsilon_{ij}}x_j)_j$ gives $|(\epsilon x)_i|^2\le(\sum_j\epsilon_{ij})(\sum_j\epsilon_{ij}|x_j|^2)\le N_1\sum_j\epsilon_{ij}|x_j|^2$. Summing over $i$ and using the column sums, also at most $N_1$, yields $\|\epsilon x\|_2^2\le N_1^2\|x\|_2^2$. Hence $\rho=\|\epsilon\|_2\le N_1$.
Substituting the stable constant [F1] and $C_1=1+7^d$ from step 1.1 into the additive estimate [F2] proves $\kappa_A(BA)\le C_{\rm FE}(1+(H/\delta)^2)(1+7^d)$.

Substituting [F1], step 1.1, and $\rho\le11^d$ from step 1.2 into the multiplicative estimate [F2] gives the displayed contraction factor. Its denominator is finite and positive, and the multiplicative theorem proves the factor is nonnegative and strictly below one. The bound is uniform as $h\to0$ and the subdomain count grows whenever $H/\delta$ stays bounded.

$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(T)=\inf_{x\ne0}\frac{a(Tx,x)}{a(x,x)},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(T)=\sup_{x\ne0}\frac{a(Tx,x)}{a(x,x)},\qquad \kappa_A(T)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}^A(T)}{\lambda_{\min}^A(T)}. $$
Then the exact additive Schwarz operator $T=BA$ is $A$-self-adjoint positive and
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(BA)\ge C_0^{-1},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(BA)\le C_1,\qquad \kappa_A(BA)\le C_0C_1. $$
If the inexact local matrices satisfy
$\alpha A_i\preceq\widetilde A_i\preceq\beta A_i$ for
$0<\alpha\le\beta$, then
$$ \lambda_{\min}^A(\widetilde BA)\ge(\beta C_0)^{-1},\qquad \lambda_{\max}^A(\widetilde BA)\le C_1/\alpha,\qquad \kappa_A(\widetilde BA)\le(\beta/\alpha)C_0C_1. $$

Work in exact real arithmetic. Let $n\ge1$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$, and let
$A=A^{\mathsf T}$ satisfy $x^{\mathsf T}Ax>0$ for every nonzero $x$.
Give $V$ the energy inner product $a(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ and norm
$\|x\|_A^2=a(x,x)$ of
[[def-energy-inner-product-and-norm-for-a-hermitian-positive-definite-matrix]].
An operator $S$ is $A$-self-adjoint when $a(Sx,y)=a(x,Sy)$ for all $x,y$;
it is positive when $a(Sx,x)>0$ for every nonzero $x$. An $A$-orthogonal
projection is an idempotent $A$-self-adjoint operator.
Let $\mathcal I$ be a finite ordered nonempty set and, for each
$i\in\mathcal I$, choose a full-column-rank prolongation
$R_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times n_i}$ with $1\le n_i\le n$, and put
$V_i=\operatorname{Ran}(R_i)$.
A one-level method has $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. A two-level method has
$\mathcal I=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$, where $R_0=P$ and $V_0$ is the designated
coarse space. Restriction of a global residual is $R_i^{\mathsf T}$ and
prolongation of a local coefficient vector is $R_i$. Define the local energy
matrix
$$A_i=R_i^{\mathsf T}AR_i.$$
When the coarse index $0$ is present, $A_0=P^{\mathsf T}AP$ is the Galerkin
coarse matrix of [[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]]. By
[[thm-galerkin-coarse-correction-is-energy-orthogonal-projector]], it is SPD
and the exact coarse solve is well-defined.

For each $i\in\mathcal I$, the exact local correction and additive
preconditioner are
$$ \Pi_i=R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}A, \qquad B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_iA_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
When the spaces span $V$, the exact additive Schwarz preconditioned operator
is $BA=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\Pi_i$. For a fixed ordering of $\mathcal I$, a
multiplicative sweep applies its corrections in that order; if $0$ is present,
it is first. For an inexact additive method, replace each exact $A_i^{-1}$ by
the inverse of an SPD matrix $\widetilde A_i$ satisfying, for fixed
$0<\alpha\le\beta$,
$$ \alpha A_i\preceq \widetilde A_i\preceq\beta A_i, \qquad \widetilde B=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}R_i\widetilde A_i^{-1}R_i^{\mathsf T}. $$
For symmetric matrices, $X\preceq Y$ means
$z^{\mathsf T}Xz\le z^{\mathsf T}Yz$ for every vector $z$. The order
inequalities define uniform local spectral equivalence in this pair. The
lemma [[lem-schwarz-local-matrices-are-well-defined]] proves the remaining
local inverse and well-definedness claims.
